rowsHeld.reason: Wet is a second correct answer. Warm is a mild form of hot exactly as damp is a mild form of wet, so damp:wet is the closest parallel to warm:hot; soaked would parallel something like scorching. The key is defensible but not the only correct option, and a child who answers wet has reasoned correctly. Change the pair (e.g. warm:scorching) or replace wet.

Sniffle is ambiguous for a child: its everyday sense is the noise of a cold ("the sniffles"), and read that way sneeze is the bigger nasal noise, so the stem has two readings and the key depends on the crying sense. Roar as a laugh (roar with laughter) also relies on a figurative sense. Use an unambiguous crying word (e.g. whimper) as the stem.

Note is also a part of a symphony, so a child applying "is a part of" (which is what novel:chapter shows) finds two correct options. What separates movement is that it is a named section like a chapter, which needs specialist musical vocabulary most 9-11 year olds will not have; the child who does not know movement will choose the part they do know. Replace note or the stem pair.

Country is a defensible second answer: a dictionary is full of words as an atlas is full of countries, and an atlas is organised by country as a dictionary is by word. Map is the better answer but not the only correct one. Replace country with a clearly wrong distractor.
Mercy is a second correct answer: mercy is an opposite of cruelty (merciful vs cruel) just as bravery is the opposite of cowardice. Replace mercy.

Dune is a defensible second answer: a grain of sand is a tiny piece of a dune just as a drop is a tiny piece of the ocean. Desert matches the vast scale of ocean better, but the row asks for the same relationship, which dune also satisfies. Replace dune.

The first pair is loose: hesitate and act are not clean opposites, so the child must guess the relationship. Read as "hold back from doing", doubt holds back from accepting as much as from believing, so accept is also correct. Use a clean antonym or cause pair and replace accept.
